title: daftar — its mechanisms, drawn

levels.meaning: what the drawn thing does and what it is built from, for someone who has never touched it: its purpose, three to five stages in the order work flows, its outcome, and each technology's own documentation. No address, port or live value

how the parts co-operate, where the work is decided and where it is fragile: parts by what they do, flows as verbs, decisions as gates, boundaries where ownership or network changes. No address or live value

what the person on call must know first, now: the drawn thing's own vital sign in a shape native to it (a row of `view_archetypes`), the evidence beneath it, what the page cannot see, and where a person may act
what exactly the parts are and how that is known: a card of each part's own facts with their provenance, the steps, the wiring, and what is still open

mechanisms.title: The gate
mechanisms.claim: A commit is recorded only if the gate passes it.

questions.orient: What keeps a wrong fact out of the notebook?
questions.understand: Where is a commit refused, and on what?
questions.operate: Is the gate refusing what it should, right now?
questions.inspect: Which hook runs which program, on what?

operate.why_none: a funnel counts the commits that arrive, those stopped at each check and those recorded; this garden exports no count of its hook's verdicts, and no monitor reads one

mechanisms.title: The journal
mechanisms.claim: Every change carries who, when and why, and no hand types the when.

questions.understand: Why can no one type a heading?
questions.operate: Is every change journalled as it is made?
questions.inspect: Where is each heading recorded, and who reads it?

operate.why_none: a roster shows who writes, and how much, from a live series; nothing here measures the journal

mechanisms.title: The merge
mechanisms.claim: Two records of one thing become one, and nothing either said is lost.

questions.orient: What happens when two records of one thing meet?
questions.understand: What decides that two beans are one object?
questions.operate: Is any merge waiting for a person?
questions.inspect: Which lines route a merge, and where?

operate.why_none: a merge waiting for a person is a fact of the ledger, merge_open on the bean, which the gate reads; it is not a metric

mechanisms.title: Peering
mechanisms.claim: What passes between gardens is only ever a proposal, and only its gardener lets it in.

questions.orient: How do two people's notebooks share one agreement?
questions.understand: Where does a proposal stop, and who lets it in?
questions.operate: What is waiting to be taken?
questions.inspect: What does a proposal carry, and where is it kept?

operate.why_none: what waits to be taken is a proposal file beside the gardens, not a metric

mechanisms.title: The ledger
mechanisms.claim: What one person owes another is read from what moved, never written.

questions.orient: Who owes whom, and how do we know?
questions.understand: Where is what is owed computed, and why is it never stored?
questions.inspect: Which transactions make up what is owed?

operate.why_none: what falls due next is answered on demand by bin/dmstale.py and bin/dmledger.py, not by a metric

cannot: Operate reads live data. The demo garden has no probe, no metric and no monitor, so every drawing takes the health chain and binds nothing, and every part reads “no signal”, with the reason: that is the demo garden's true state.
Actions: none is placed. A button in the report asks for a tool by name, and only a host's own configuration can make it run anything.
Author edits a copy of the page's record in the reader's browser. What it exports is imported into a garden by a command run in that garden; nothing imports it here.
The served page, and a monitor's dashboards, are not part of this site.
